intro_html: Five spice powder is one of those seasonings that does more work than it has any right to: star anise, cinnamon, clove, fennel, and pepper in one spoonful. Here it seasons ground turkey and mushrooms in a brothy noodle bowl finished with hot honey, which brings sweet heat to the back end. Each bowl comes to 561 calories and 34 grams of protein for about $2.57.
cost_closing_html: About $2.57 a bowl for a noodle bowl with real depth to it. The five spice jar in your cabinet is what makes the difference, and it costs pennies per serving.
shop_smart: Mushrooms are the second biggest line here. Buy them the day they get marked down, because slightly wrinkled mushrooms actually taste more concentrated once they hit a hot pan.

Broth is a real line for this batch because a noodle bowl drinks a lot of it. Bouillon base dissolved in water costs a fraction of the carton price and disappears completely into a bowl this seasoned.
Hot honey is the fun ingredient and one bottle covers this batch three times over. If you already own honey and red pepper flakes, you can build your own and skip the specialty bottle entirely.
Five spice powder runs a few dollars a jar and lasts a year of cooking. Buy it at an international market where the same jar often costs half what the grocery store spice aisle charges.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the mushrooms thick. Thin slices vanish into a broth like this, and you want them to stay recognizable in the bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes without stirring much, so they release their water and then start to brown instead of steam.
Add the minced garlic and the five spice powder and stir for one minute. This blooming step wakes the spice up, and it is the whole reason this bowl tastes like more than salty broth.
Pour in the chicken broth, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer 15 minutes so the flavors marry.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat and taste. It should read savory first and sweet second.
Boil the lo mein noodles just short of done, drain them, rinse them cold so they stop cooking, and move them into your weighed pot.
portion_html: Set the pot of noodles on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is the noodle bed for each container. Ladle the turkey, mushrooms, and broth evenly across all 14 and top each with sliced green onions. Every bowl lands at 561 calories and 34 grams of protein.

steps: Brown the ground turkey in olive oil to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes until browned.
Add garlic and five spice powder and bloom one minute, then add the chicken broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat.
Cook and rinse the noodles, portion by weight into 14 containers, and ladle the broth over the top.
